verticals.description: Probes whether a confirmed authenticated identity can reach, read, or write an object, property, or function outside its own ownership or role boundary: object-level bypass (IDOR, BOLA), object-property-level bypass (BOPLA — reading undisclosed properties or writing properties a caller shouldn't control, such as a `role` field in a write request), and function-level bypass (BFLA), each checked both horizontally (same privilege tier, a different owner's data) and vertically (a lower-privileged identity reaching a higher-privileged action), plus whether an auth-gated input enforces identity at all versus enforcing it incorrectly. Dispatches every probe through `curl.get` (an object-id in a `path_segment` or `query` value) or `curl.post_form` (an object-id or property in `data`), carrying each probing identity's credential in `headers`. Use when the Workspace's enumerated surface carries an object-id-shaped input (a numeric or UUID path segment, an `id`/`*_id`-named query parameter or hidden form field), a property-bearing write endpoint (a PUT/PATCH/POST body), or a role-gated endpoint, and the Workspace has credentials for at least two distinct Target identities. Do not use for a resource that was never gated behind authentication at all (a genuinely public endpoint) — that's the `information disclosure` vertical. Do not use for the session token or cookie itself being guessable, forgeable, or otherwise weak — that's `auth/session`.
verticals.name: access-control

verticals.description: Probes the Target's session-management and authentication-flow mechanics for logic flaws that let a session, token, or verification step outlive or escape the boundary it should be scoped to: session fixation (a pre-chosen session identifier remains valid after authentication), missing session invalidation on logout, credential change, account disable/lockout, or an explicit "log out all devices" control (an old session identifier still grants access afterward), weak session-cookie and persistent-login ("remember me") token attributes, password-reset token weaknesses (predictability, reuse after redemption, missing expiration), and multi-factor verification-binding weaknesses (the server not re-checking the second factor server-side, or checking it against the wrong account). Dispatches through `curl.get`/`curl.post_form`, reading the session identifier and its attributes off the leading status-line and header block their output carries, and setting a chosen session value via `headers`. Use when recon has confirmed a session-identifying cookie or header and a login endpoint on the Workspace's surface. Do not use for a request replayed cross-site using the victim's own ambient session — that's `CSRF`. Do not use for brute-forcing or rate-limiting a login, OTP, or reset endpoint — that's the reserved `rate-limiting / brute-force` vertical. Do not use for a JWT's own signing or structure weaknesses, an OAuth flow's own weaknesses, or a reset link poisoned via the Host header or a forwarded-host header (e.g. `X-Forwarded-Host`) — that's the reserved `OAuth / JWT handling` or `Host header attacks` vertical respectively.
verticals.name: auth-session

verticals.description: Probes every discovered input for command, SQL, LDAP, XPath, template (SSTI), header/CRLF, and NoSQL injection by submitting a canonical boundary-breaking payload per class and diffing the observed response against a clean baseline. Use when recon has enumerated at least one request-shaped input (form field, query parameter, header, cookie, path segment, or uploaded filename) on any Workspace. Do not use for deserialization of structured payloads (pickle, YAML, XML, Java-object streams) — that's the `deserialization` vertical; this one is for payloads interpreted as code or query syntax, never payloads reconstructed as a data structure.
verticals.name: injection

verticals.description: Enumerates every request-shaped input the Target exposes (form fields, query parameters, headers, cookies, path segments, upload filenames) and attempts to confirm or refute every gate signal a gated vertical declares, recording both to the Workspace's shared surface. Use when a Workspace's Playbook starts, before any other vertical's own investigation begins. Do not use for judging what a discovered input means for a specific weakness class, or for probing it — that's every offensive vertical's own job; this one only maps what the Target exposes and never claims a weakness of its own.
verticals.name: recon

verticals.description: Probes whether any input controls, in whole or part, the destination of a server-initiated outbound request — a URL, hostname, IP, or path fragment used by a webhook/callback, a fetch-by-URL feature, an image proxy, or a PDF/report generator — letting the Target be made to issue a request to an attacker-chosen destination (localhost, an internal-only host, a cloud metadata endpoint) instead of, or in addition to, its intended one. Dispatches through `curl.get`'s `query`/`path_segment`/`headers` or `curl.post_form`'s `data`, submitting a tiered set of destinations and reading the status/header block and elapsed-time line their output carries. Use when the Workspace's surface records an input whose name or recorded normal value is URL/hostname-shaped, whose baseline response already shows the Target fetching content from that value, or a `Referer` header the Target's own back-end processes. Do not use for a path or filename read directly off local disk — that's `file handling`. Do not use for a request forged cross-site using the victim's own browser session — that's `CSRF`. Do not use for scanning the Target's own listening ports directly — that's `recon`'s job; this vertical is about the Target making a request on the attacker's behalf, not the attacker reaching the Target itself. Do not use for a URL embedded inside a parsed structured payload (XML, YAML, or similar) that a parser dereferences as part of handling the format itself — that's the `deserialization` vertical's territory, not a destination-naming input this vertical enumerates directly.
verticals.name: ssrf
